subject: BioVanta: post-call architecture summary + SLA outline
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@biovanta.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.inference.com, priyom_das@redwood.inference.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: BioVanta post-call: architecture summary + recommended SLA targets

Elena — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have a shared picture and clear next steps.

Key pain / goals (as I heard them):
- Latency-sensitive inference for patient-facing clinical hints (95th pct target ~150ms).
- Strong isolation requirement: PHI data must not be mixed with other tenants (VPC + dedicated GPUs).
- Predictable throughput for nightly batch scoring (up to 80k tokens/min peak) and spiky daytime API traffic.
- SOC2 evidence / procurement checklist to close in 3–4 weeks.

Redwood recommended configuration (initial):
- Dedicated pool: 4x A100-equivalent GPUs reserved (sliced into two private islands for dev vs prod).
- Isolation: VPC + customer-managed KMS; optional on-prem connector if needed later.
- Scaling: autoscale buffer + burst policy for daytime spikes (50% headroom above baseline).
- SLA targets: 99.5% uptime for the dedicated pool; median token latency ~40–60ms; 95th pct SLA (app-level) target 180ms.

Immediate next steps (for this week):
1) I will share a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP) draft and our SOC2 questionnaire.
2) Elena — if you can loop in procurement and confirm the SOW timeline and any legal redlines we should be aware of.
3) Rishi / Priyom — I flagged a couple of options on instance sizing for the model sizing exercise (sketches attached).

Attachments: draft-MAP-biovanta.xlsx (MAP with milestones); model-sizing-notes.txt (inline in email thread).

If any of the bullets above don't match your notes, flag and I'll adjust. Otherwise I'll send the MAP + questionnaire within the hour.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.inference.com | +1 (415) 555-0178

From: Elena Morales <elena@biovanta.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: procurement@biovanta.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 16:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BioVanta post-call: architecture summary + recommended SLA targets

Ben — this captures it well, thanks. A few clarifications / asks from our side:

Clarifications:
- The 95th pct latency target is for interactive clinical UI calls; background batch can be relaxed.
- For isolation, we need the ability to audit access logs quarterly and export key rotation logs to our KMS.

Requests:
- Can you provide a short ops runbook (1–2 pages) showing failover if the dedicated pool loses a node? Procurement will want "how we stay online" language.
- SOC2 questionnaire: procurement asked for the latest evidence bundle and a point-of-contact for the security review.

Procurement is on this thread (procurement@biovanta.com). They requested: estimated first-year cost range, a draft SOW timeline, and a list of required procurement inputs (PO format, billing contact, required SOC artifacts).

I'll review the MAP once you send it. We aim to have procurement feedback by 05/27.

—Elena
Elena Morales
Head of Platform Operations | BioVanta
elena@biovanta.com | +1 (617) 555-3344

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@biovanta.com>, procurement@biovanta.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.inference.com, priyom_das@redwood.inference.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 17:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BioVanta post-call: architecture summary + recommended SLA targets

Elena / procurement team — attaching the SOC2 questionnaire and a draft MAP for your review. Quick notes inline: see attached draft-MAP-biovanta.xlsx.

Budget band (ballpark):
- Reserved 4x A100-eq pool with isolation + baseline monitoring: $85k–$110k / month (depends on sustained throughput and optional on-prem connector).
- One-time onboarding professional services (ops playbook, runbook, initial model optimization): $18k–$30k.

Ops/runbook highlights (high level):
- Failover path: automatic routing to standby nodes inside the dedicated pool; if pool capacity is consumed, traffic temporarily routes to a warmed compatible model on our regional standby cluster with degraded latency guarantees.
- Auditability: we expose per-token request logs (redacted PHI) and KMS rotation events via secure log export. Quarterly audit exports can be generated on request.

Proposed SLA language (starter):
- 99.5% availability for the dedicated GPU pool (monthly measurement).
- 95th pct application latency SLO: 180ms (best-effort on bursts and fallback events).
- Credits: pro-rata credit for downtime > SLA threshold; to be finalized in SOW.

Next steps (action owners):
- Ben: finalize MAP + send SOC2 bundle (this email).
- Elena: share procurement's preferred invoice/billing details and any legal must-haves by 2027-05-27.
- Rishi: schedule a 1-hour model sizing session with BioVanta engineering (target next Tue).

Attachments: BioVanta_SOC2_Questionnaire.pdf, draft-MAP-biovanta.xlsx (MAP includes milestones & SOW draft).

Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference.com>

Subject: Fwd: BioVanta post-call: architecture summary + SLA outline — internal next steps

Forwarding BioVanta thread — high priority. Procurement expects numbers and the runbook/ops language by EOD Friday so they can prep their vendor packet. Notes for you two:

1) Rishi: prioritize the model sizing session. Bring the quantization/latency numbers for the 4x pool options (we discussed 4x vs 6x tradeoffs).
2) Priyom: draft a concise ops-runbook (1–2 pages) describing failover flow and audit export steps. Include a diagram stub — simple ASCII is fine.
3) I'll own the MAP updates and the initial cost band; want to keep the top-of-range conservative so procurement doesn't push back.

I'll loop legal if procurement identifies redlines; otherwise we'll keep this as a standard SOW with addenda for audit requirements.

-ben
